cfu.question: Which object can show a fact about a rock: a safe sample or a food picture?

hinge.question: A class claims a clean plastic lid floats. Which evidence could check the claim?

options.text: A photo of a different lid.
options.diagnosis: A different item is not direct evidence for this lid.

options.text: A guess from the lid colour.
options.diagnosis: Colour alone does not test floating.
Evidence about another item misses the claim.

options.text: A safe water test of that lid.
options.diagnosis: Selects a direct safe observation of the claimed behaviour.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model I point to the bone model. It shows a skeleton. The bones help hold the body up. Ask the parallel hinge. No scores or answers saved.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A pupil claims a toy rolls farther on a smooth mat. What evidence could check it? Compare measured rolls from the same start on two mats.

misconceptions.misconception: A picture is proof of a rock hardness result.
misconceptions.spot: Offers a food or generic rock picture as a test result.
misconceptions.correction: Use an actual safe sample or genuine recorded result from a completed test.

misconceptions.misconception: A skeleton model and a rock sample answer the same question.
misconceptions.spot: Uses one item for every claim.
misconceptions.correction: Match each question to a relevant model or observation.

we_do.support: Point to one model. What can it show?
we_do.stretch: Which fact needs a new check rather than a card?

tiers.F: Show one fact about a body or rock.
tiers.M: Show two facts. Tell how you found one.
tiers.H: Pick your best real evidence. Why does it fit?
tiers.go_deeper: Pick a claim you cannot show. What could you check?
tiers.early_finisher: Pick the best real result. Why does it fit?

adaptations.cognition_learning: Give a three-step visual card for show what we know about bodies and rocks; remove its last cue after a correct try.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Point to the real kit before a short spoken, signed or AAC response; wait for a turn.
adaptations.semh: Offer a private first–then cue and planned pause before the hinge; re-enter with one step.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Use a stable tray, large cards or an accessible input; no forced touch.
adaptations.eal: Rehearse a full M or H idea in any language before writing; keep the science challenge.

facts.claim: A skeleton supports, protects and helps the body move.
Rock samples can be compared by appearance and simple physical properties.
A model or card represents an idea; only actual observed work supports a claim about a particular test result.
Vocabulary term skeleton means bones that help hold a body up; example: I point to the bone model.
Vocabulary term nutrition means what a body gets from food to grow and stay well; example: An animal gets nutrition from food.
Vocabulary term rock means a solid thing from the ground; example: I can test a safe rock.
Vocabulary term evidence means what you saw or did that helps show a claim; example: My rock sort shows my rule.
Retrieval question from SoW C44: What stays the same in a fair water test? Answer: The drops and waiting time.
Retrieval question from SoW C43: Is a finished brick raw or made? Answer: It is human-made.
Retrieval question from SoW C38: Where do animals get food? Answer: From what they eat.
The “Skeleton” drawing shows bones that support the body and help protect organs.
The “Food” drawing shows an apple; animals get nutrition from food.
The “Rock” drawing is an illustration for comparing a sample's appearance, not an observed result.
New transfer hinge and parallel: A class claims a clean plastic lid floats. Which evidence could check the claim? Correct: A safe water test of that lid.

stages: Arrival (5 min): Pick a safe model or card to look at. Staff: Offer a safe kit choice and short first–then cue.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say, sign or point. Staff: Ask three low-stakes prior questions; answers in note.
I Do (5 min): Watch one fact with one clue. Staff: Pre-teach words; show the full model; ask the show-me check.
We Do (7 min): Match a real model to a fact. Staff: Hand over the missing step; offer F or H route. Reset once.
We Do 2 (5 min): Choose one answer. All of us show it. Staff: Take all pupil responses at once; use decision rule and parallel hinge.
Independent (8 min): Show work you did about body, food or rock. Staff: Choose one adult for supported pupils, one for group; swap across the week.
Review (4 min): Hear one next step. Fix a part if you can. Staff: Give VF and one NS(+); invite one self-edit. Reset once.
Exit (3 min): Tell an adult what you know and how. Staff: Hear feedback and next step, choose next start, then one-minute reset.
